historical_anchor: Turner late-Nov 1943 lessons: more reconnaissance/submarine scouting, obstacle demolition, destroyers, landing craft, and roughly triple pre-landing bombardment/ammunition; Spruance approved in early Dec.

branch_information_model.rule: US adapts to what it observes, not to hidden Branch parameters.
likely_immediate_beliefs: pre-assault damage assessment was too optimistic
Japanese protected positions and local C2 survived longer than expected
support shipping needs stronger surface/submarine/air defense
not_immediately_known: precise Japanese shipping reserve and rear-airfield completion state

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more ammunition, longer fires, more observed re-attacks
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: BB/CA/DD ship-days, ammunition lift, fuel, target spotting, submarine exposure; smoke/dust can degrade observation and landing control

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more photo-recon, repeat strikes, tighter target-system attack
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: carrier deck cycles, CAP/search/ASW/anti-carrier reserve; small-atoll airspace and target-identification congestion

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more LVT/LVT(A), better obstacle/recon lanes, more reserve lift
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: APA/LST deck space, reef/lagoon traffic control, beach exits, maintenance/fuel; extra craft do not create extra beach frontage

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more integrated reduction teams and on-call fire
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: beach unloading priority, engineer equipment, artillery ammo, road/exits and command bandwidth

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more DD on-call gunfire and outer pickets
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: same hull cannot simultaneously provide shore fire, ASW, radar picket and anti-surface screen

adaptation_axes.natural_response: more aerial/submarine reconnaissance and obstacle reconnaissance
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: recon can telegraph objective and give Japan time to disperse/reinforce; tension with surprise

adaptation_axes.natural_response: amass more lift/support before next assault
adaptation_axes.finite_cost: calendar delay gives Japan more construction time and permits carrier/air-group regeneration; delay is not automatically beneficial

target_choice_effect: Heavier Tarawa losses do not automatically force a Wotje/Maloelap stepping-stone assault. Historically caution increased yet Nimitz chose direct Kwajalein. In Branch B, stronger outer-island fortifications can make bypass more attractive, while harder-to-suppress aviation can make bypass more dangerous. Reopen target choice after Jan air/hardening and fleet-cover ledgers are closed.
congestion_rule: Once firepower/lift exceed local command, spotting, airspace, reef lanes, beach exits, fuel/ammunition handling or radio capacity, marginal added force produces delay/friendly-fire/queueing rather than proportional combat power.
